description: Argues that accurate metrics can become misleading objectives; develops three mechanisms (gaming, selection on noise, and incomplete proxies), the history of Goodhart and Campbell, a Wells Fargo case, and independent checks on institutional goals.

related_resources.reason: Original author revisits the monetary-policy warning about targeting formerly predictive indicators.
Early source for the pressure and corruption problems in quantitative social-program evaluation.
Historical attribution of related but not identical laws and the later slogan.
Documented enforcement case used to distinguish real institutional failure from invented illustrations.

historical_claims.anchor: Goodhart developed this point in the mid-1970s.
historical_claims.source_locator: Goodhart (2006), abstract and original-formulation reference; Green (2018), historical comparison

historical_claims.anchor: That slogan is a later, broader formulation associated with the anthropologist Marilyn Strathern, drawing on earlier discussion by Keith Hoskin.
Donald Campbell, writing about social programs in the same period, approached a neighboring problem.
historical_claims.source_locator: 1976 occasional paper bibliographic record; 1979 journal version

historical_claims.anchor: In September 2016, the United States Consumer Financial Protection Bureau announced an enforcement action against Wells Fargo.
historical_claims.source_locator: CFPB September 8, 2016 press release and linked consent order

claim_evidence.anchor: The bank's own analysis, cited at the time, identified more than two million accounts that may not have been authorized.
claim_evidence.source_locator: CFPB September 8, 2016 press release, first paragraph
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Potentially unauthorized figure; explicit uncertainty preserved.

claim_evidence.anchor: The regulator imposed a one-hundred-million-dollar civil penalty, alongside other actions.
claim_evidence.source_locator: CFPB September 8, 2016 press release, announcement and penalty details
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: CFPB penalty distinguished from other concurrent financial sanctions.

authorship.scope: Original argumentative essay and its fictional examples; research-based history and enforcement case supported by bibliography.

background: No assumed mathematics. The technical ideas of overfitting and selection bias are introduced in ordinary language.
readiness_checks: Explain how a metric may be accurately recorded yet fail to capture the value it stands for.
Distinguish deliberate gaming, selection on noisy scores, and displacement of unmeasured values.
Give a reason for using independent evaluation rather than abandoning measurement.
